reviews.review: really fun to play with frineds

Your a space ninja.
Nuff said.

I first played this game a very very long time ago, I believe when it was in beta, or some form of early access.

I'd been looking for an MMO of some kind to get into, but was absolutely bored with everything I'd been seeing online so far. Games like World of WarCraft dominated the MMO landscape. A High Fantasy Adventure in Medieval Knights-And-Magic-World #365? Ugh. No thanks.

I've always been a sci-fi guy. I prefer my adventures to take place in space, or the future, and involve robots and lasers. Magic? Wizards? Knights on horseback? Elves? Dwarves? Orcs? Goblins? Seen it. Boring. Pass.

Then I heard about this WarFrame game and it IMMEDIATELY called to me. Just reading about it, it felt like it ticked all my boxes.

Sci-fi theme? Check.
Action, reflex-based combat? Check.
Not explicitly guns-only combat? Double Check.

You'd think that last one is a wierd one but melee is very important to me. I love melee combat and there seemed to be very few games, if ANY, at the time that were willing to mix it into a sci-fi theme, let alone a modern one.

So I jumped on it at the earliest opportunity.

(Originally, there was a story here about my experiences playing WarFrame the first time, but I cut it out to make my review short enough to be accepted)

After a rocky start, I quickly grew to love WarFrame for many reasons. Now I'm eagerly awaiting a new content update that is going to let me have an NPC crew on board my RailJack for thrilling ship-to-ship space combat adventures.

It's not perfect. In fact, it's riddled with flaws, especially some that seem to only get worse over time. But in spite of that, I would urge anyone reading this to give it a try. Especially now after the "New Player Experience" has been retooled a few times to not be as incredibly hostile as it used to be.

There are things to not love about this game, sure. It can often get VERY grindy, and as if the grind wasn't bad enough there are timegates to obtaining most things that just so happen to allow you to skip them if you're willing to spend Platinum, the game's premium currency that is obtainable via cash purchase, and it can often feel like the gamedevs are purposely nudging you towards doing exactly that to avoid putting up with their shenanigans.

Power Creep is a major problem in the game, with old things quickly losing relevance/viability as time marches on and new, more powerful gear is introduced, and there is so much content that the devs struggle to keep up with fixing and updating all the things that need to be fixed and updated that many players have lost patience and quit over the years.

In spite of this, I would urge you to try this game. In spite of this, there are many things to love about it.

I could go into detail about everything that WarFrame does well, but I think for me personally, I'd like to just talk about the three things I love the most about it: The Gameplay, the Aesthetics, and the Story.

First, let's talk gameplay. WarFrame is THRILLING.

My character steps into a large, quiet room and sees two Grineer officers standing atop a walled structure, sort of like a balcony overlooking a door into another area. They haven't noticed that he's here. He charges forward along the ground, leaps like superman SEVERAL feet into the sky. By the time they see him, it's too late. He's diving straight at them with a giant broadsword in hand and whirling around cleaving neatly through both soldiers in one slice before he hits the ground. In that split second he notices several more soldiers are now looking at him in another room ahead that wasn't visible from the ground floor level, and in response he thrusts his fist into the floor and a wave of freezing icicles bursts forth from the ground under their feet, stabbing at them with sharp, icy spines and slowing them down considerably. This gives him time to reload his shotgun before he starts gunning them down one by one. They shoot him a few times, but with their weak bullets and insanely reduced movement and attack speed from the layers of freeze coating them, the damage is negligible. Non-existent, really.

And most importantly, that was not a cutscene. That was a thing I actually did.

What I love most about WarFrame's gameplay isn't just how good it feels to control your character, perform amazing stunts and rack up kills with incredibly flashy moves. What I love is that you have such a wide variety of options for how you play the game.

Not only do different WarFrames (your battle suits) have unique ability loadouts that make them play differently (so there's bound to be one that appeals to your playstyle), but the basic mechanics of the game provide you options: You can gun down your enemies, you can snipe or stab them in the back un-noticed and ninja your way through a mission, you can go full berserker melee and mow down hordes with your trusty blade, or you can play the wizard, and spam your abilities to make your foes bend to your awesome power. It's almost like you get to choose what kind of game you're playing: First Person Shooter? Hack and Slash? Stealth, or maybe even whatever Diablo is technically classified as?

I tend to be the Berserker Melee, but I like to be a Stealth Assassin or Power Spammer on occasion. The thing is, I have the CHOICE, and that's incredible.

And now we get to the Story. I think WarFrame is my FAVORITE story in any game ever made. I'm daunted thinking about how I'm going to describe this to you without spoiling too much... I think all I can say is that there are some amazing twists and the lore is VERY rich and well-thought-out. There are small details to look at everywhere and each faction of the game has it's own worldbuilding and power structure to analyze, which is enhanced by the game's powerful aesthetics.

... I actually think that for the sake of conserving your experience with the story, I can't say much more than that, so I'll transition into talking about the aesthetics after all.

As I said before, part of the reason I was drawn to this game is because I was desperate for an action/adventure MMO with a sci-fi twist, and WarFrame KNOWS it's target audience. Everywhere you go, you really feel like you're in some wild futuristic space adventure across the stars. Even on Earth, which now looks like some kind of alien, overgrown jungle planet riddled with ruined Grineer base structures. For me, my favorite places to be are either on Corpus Ships, or in old Orokin Towers. Corpus bases and locations have exactly the kind of futuristic sci-fi aesthetic I love, where everything is metallic and glowing with power and data, robots and mechanisms galore! And old, abandoned Orokin towers successfully pull off that feeling of an ancient race of super-advanced aliens who had technology beyond our comprehension. Even the Grineer tilesets, which are my least favorite, have an element of futuristic sci-fi feel to them. I like to call their aesthetic "Junk Tech". It looks more... bulbous, industrial and... honestly less like competent machines and more like trash jammed together, but even that can be charming in a way.

I love exploring the areas in this game and if you love sci-fi aesthetics I think you will, too.

But I think the most important reason you should try this game is, well...

... it's free!

Free to download, free to play, free to win, absolutely free. All the way. You don't have to drop a dime if you don't want to, and if it ever gets to a point where it just seems like far too much annoyance to be worth it, it's also free to UN-install.

I can't think of a better reason to recommend this game than "It's free, and it's not total ♥♥♥♥".

But maybe... that's just me.
